summary: Friends Calendar is a full-stack real-time collaborative calendar and messaging web application. It enables friends and groups to manage shared calendars, chat in real-time, and store shared memories (posts with descriptions and images). The backend is built with Node.js, Express, MongoDB (Mongoose), and Socket.IO, while the frontend is built with React, Vite, Material-UI, and Socket.IO client.
projectStructure: backend/ - Node.js Express server with Socket.IO and Mongoose models
backend/controllers/ - Controller logic for authentication, events, groups, memories, and messages
backend/middleware/ - Auth guards, error handling, file uploads, and request validation
backend/models/ - Mongoose schemas for User, Group, Event, Memory, Message, and Friendship
backend/routes/ - Express API endpoints routing to controllers
frontend/src/api/ - Axios client instance and API configuration
frontend/src/components/ - Reusable UI components (Button, Calendar, Header, Modal)
frontend/src/context/ - React Context providers for Auth, Events, Friends, and Memories
frontend/src/features/ - Feature-specific React components (categories, events, friends, memories)
frontend/src/pages/ - Main application pages (Chat, Comments, Home, Login, Register, Profile, MyCalendar)
technologies: Vite (v7.2.4) - Frontend build tool and development server
Node.js & Express (v5.2.1) - Backend API server, utilizing Express 5 for native async error handling
MongoDB & Mongoose (v9.1.2) - Database and Object Data Modeling (ODM) library
Axios (v1.13.5) - HTTP client for API communication
Material-UI (MUI v7.3.6) & Material Pickers - UI components and calendar controls
Multer (v2.1.0) - Multipart form data parser for uploading avatars and memory photos
strengths: Express 5 adoption allows native async error handling, reducing repetitive try-catch blocks in route handlers.
Well-structured dynamic relationships in Mongoose using refPath to easily link events and memories to both Friendships and Groups.
Efficient search indexing on User schema (username/fullName text indexes) and Memory schema (tags, text indexes on title/description/place).
Decoupled React architecture separating context state logic from presentation components.
Responsive styling for major features like calendar, chat, and memories with clean separation of CSS and JSX.
issues: Broken Add Member Payload: In FriendsContext.jsx, addMembersToGroup sends { userIds }, but backend groupController.js expects { members }, resulting in newMembers being [undefined] and throwing a Mongoose CastError on save, breaking the add member feature.

Critical Socket.IO Impersonation vulnerability: The WebSocket server does not authenticate connections or verify the JWT. The send-message event trusts client-supplied senderId and senderInfo, allowing any client to send messages impersonating any user.

Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA/IDOR) on group messages: GET /api/messages?groupId=id does not check if req.user is a member of the requested group, permitting any authenticated user to read all messages from any group.

Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA/IDOR) on events: POST /api/events creates events for any Friendship or Group without checking if the creator is actually a member, allowing unauthorized event injections.

Schema-Logic Mismatch on Categories: Group categories schema is defined as categories: [ { type: [String] } ], making it an array of subdocuments. But backend groupController.js checks if a category is present using group.categories.includes(category) (which checks if an array of objects contains a string). This check always returns false, leading to duplicate category insertions and querying failures.

Mismatched Group validation: validateGroupInput in validation.js validates 'title' instead of 'name'. Since the frontend sends 'name', the group name length and format are never validated, rendering the middleware ineffective.

Missing Schema fields for password resets: getResetPasswordToken in User.js sets resetPasswordToken and resetPasswordExpire on the Mongoose document, but these fields are not defined in the UserSchema, which will cause Mongoose to strip them out on save.

Frontend Axios Client Inconsistency: Bypassing the configured apiClient in FriendsContext.jsx and Chat.jsx (using vanilla axios or fetch directly) bypasses 401/403 response interceptors, preventing automated user redirection on session expiry.
Dead Frontend Dependency: Multer is listed as a frontend dependency in package.json, which is a Node.js-only library and should not reside in client bundle files.
recommendations: Align Add Member payload: Update either FriendsContext.jsx to send { members: userIds } or update groupController.js to extract { userIds } instead of { members }.

Implement Socket.IO Authentication: Secure Socket.IO connections by implementing a middleware using socket.io's use() method to verify the JWT from the request cookie, and use the verified socket.userId in all events.
Enforce Group Membership checks: Add checks in GET /api/messages and POST /api/events to ensure the req.user.id is a member of the group/friendship being accessed or updated.
Fix Group Categories schema: Simplify categories in Group.js to categories: { type: [String], default: [] } to align with Friendship.js and ensure includes() works as expected.
Correct validation fields: Update validateGroupInput in validation.js to validate 'name' instead of 'title'.
Add fields to User Schema: Include resetPasswordToken (String) and resetPasswordExpire (Date) in the UserSchema in User.js.
Refactor frontend requests: Standardize all HTTP requests in FriendsContext.jsx and Chat.jsx to use apiClient instead of importing axios or fetch directly, ensuring consistent session management.
